title: Returns Still Owed Back to the Retailer and the Machines They Keep Out of a Renew Bulk IT Refresh Wave
content:
The machines a live return authorisation holds back follow the returns standing on the profile, because goods still owed back to the retailer are not put into a trade-in wave. The returns in question are the return authorisations the profile holds under Northbeam Returns and Restocking, and the inspections recorded against that profile's returns.

| The returns standing on the profile | Machines held back from the Renew Bulk IT Refresh wave |
| --- | --- |
| a return authorisation standing authorized, and no inspection recorded on the profile's returns within the last twelve months | the authorized return figure, 3 machines |
| a return authorisation standing received, and an inspection recorded on the profile's returns within the last twelve months | the received return figure, 1 machine |
| no return authorisation standing authorized or received | none |

**Reading the pairs.** Each of the first two rows joins a state a return authorisation stands in to what the last twelve months of inspections show. A return authorisation standing authorized on a profile whose returns carry an inspection inside the last twelve months matches neither of the first two rows, and so no machine is held back on this account; the same holds for one standing received on a profile with no inspection in those twelve months.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A profile holding a return authorisation standing authorized under Northbeam Returns and Restocking, with no inspection recorded against its returns in the last twelve months, holds 3 machines back from the wave. A profile holding one standing received, with 2 inspections recorded in those twelve months, holds 1 machine back. A profile whose only return authorisation stands in some other state holds none back.
